title: Marvell Structera X 3406 and 3506 CXL 3.2 Memory Expanders
gist: Marvell announced second-generation Structera X CXL 3.2 memory expanders (3406 for DDR4, 3506 for DDR5) with PCIe Gen6, six memory channels instead of four, and line-rate LZ4 compression, doubling host bandwidth to 256GB/s. ServeTheHome sees them as a better version of the prior generation for hyperscalers reclaiming DDR4, with six channels putting 50% more DRAM behind one controller than competitors' four.

insights.claim: Marvell's second-generation Structera X CXL memory expanders add CXL 3.2 support, PCIe Gen6 connectivity, and raise memory channels from four to six.
insights.speaker: Vic A
insights.so_what: Channel count and link speed are the core generational upgrade; track design wins at hyperscalers.
insights.quote: Marvell announced its second-generation Structera X CXL memory expanders, adding CXL 3.2 support, PCIe Gen6 connectivity, and increasing memory channels from four to six.
insights.locator: CXL has seen a massive surge recently

insights.claim: Structera X model numbers encode the spec: first digit 3 is CXL 3 (the 2 in 2404/2504 marked CXL 2.0), the second digit 4 or 5 is the DDR generation, and trailing digits are channel count, so the 3406 is CXL 3 DDR4 with six channels and the 3506 is CXL 3 DDR5 with six channels.
insights.speaker: Vic A
insights.so_what: Lets you map SKUs to memory generations at a glance when tracking Marvell's CXL lineup.
insights.locator: Marvell Structera X 3406 and 3506 CXL 3.2 Memory Expanders

insights.claim: PCIe Gen6 plus CXL 3.2 gives roughly twice the link bandwidth, which is how Marvell delivers more bandwidth from the extra memory channels.
insights.speaker: Vic A
insights.so_what: Bandwidth per expander scales with link generation, so PCIe Gen6 adoption gates CXL expander value.
insights.quote: PCIe Gen6 infrastructure and CXL 3.2 means we get roughly twice the bandwidth over the link

insights.claim: This announcement covers only the Structera X memory-expansion line, not the Structera A near-memory compute controller shown last year.
insights.speaker: Vic A
insights.so_what: No update yet on the near-memory compute product; watch for a separate Structera A refresh.
insights.locator: This announcement covers only the Structera X

insights.claim: The DDR4 Structera X 3406 runs six channels at 1600MT/s with 3DPC, taking 18 DIMMs for up to 9TB per controller, while the DDR5 3506 takes 12 DIMMs for up to 6TB.
insights.speaker: Vic A
insights.so_what: A single DDR4 controller can host up to 9TB, making large-scale reuse of older DRAM practical.
insights.quote: That lets the DDR4 part take 18 DIMMs for up to 9TB per controller, and the DDR5 3506 takes 12 DIMMs for up to 6TB.
insights.locator: Structera X 3506 pairs six DDR5 channels

insights.claim: Both new controllers stay on Marvell's 5nm process and include LZ4 compression, with the compression engine now sized to keep up with the interface (250GB/s on the 3506) so it is not a bottleneck.
insights.speaker: Vic A
insights.so_what: Line-rate compression raises effective capacity per DIMM, lowering cost per usable gigabyte.
insights.quote: In this generation, Marvell is ensuring that the LZ4 can keep up with the interface so it is not a bottleneck.
insights.locator: Both new controllers stay on Marvell’s 5nm process

insights.claim: CXL 3.2 lets up to four hosts share pooled memory with up to 256GB/s of host bandwidth, double the prior generation's 128GB/s.
insights.speaker: Vic A
insights.so_what: Memory pooling across four hosts supports hyperscaler efficiency gains from stranded-memory reduction.
insights.quote: CXL 3.2 lets up to four hosts share pooled memory, with up to 256GB/s of host bandwidth, double the prior generation’s 128GB/s.
insights.locator: Structera X 3506 pairs six DDR5 channels

themes.theme: Why CXL expanders matter amid DRAM tightness

insights.claim: CXL is aimed at optimizing either bandwidth per core, since CXL bandwidth adds to native DDR bandwidth, or capacity expansion, serving memory-intensive workloads like high-bandwidth ML/AI inference and DLRM.
insights.speaker: Vic A
insights.so_what: Two distinct buying motives (bandwidth vs capacity) imply different customer segments for expanders.
insights.quote: CXL is focused on optimizing either bandwidth per core (since CXL bandwidth is in addition to native DDR bandwidth) and also capacity expansion.

insights.claim: Line-rate LZ4 compression makes attached memory roughly half as costly per gigabyte, which makes CXL expanders attractive as AI demand tightens DRAM supply and pushes DDR5 prices up.
insights.speaker: Vic A
insights.so_what: AI-driven DRAM scarcity and rising DDR5 prices are a demand tailwind for CXL expander vendors like Marvell.
insights.quote: That hands-on look explains why CXL expanders are attractive as AI demand tightens DRAM supply and pushes DDR5 prices up.

insights.so_what: Reusing retired DDR4 via CXL is a cost lever for hyperscalers when new DRAM is expensive.
